title: Matter Can Change Chemically — Investigating Matter, Chapter 5
eyebrow: CKSci Grade 5 · Investigating Matter · Chapter 5 · Student Reader pp. 27–32
bigQuestion: Why do some interactions of matter result in new substances?

mission.name: Chapter 5 review
mission.blurb: A quick check that the chapter landed — not a test.

items.q: Ana makes a salad and Jamal bakes bread. Which is a mixture, and how can you tell?
opts: The salad — it can be taken apart to get back the same ingredients
The bread — heating always leaves the ingredients unchanged
Both, because in each one two things were put together
Neither, because both were made in a kitchen rather than a lab
items.why: A mixture is different types of matter mixed together while each type stays unchanged, so it can be separated back into its original parts. You can take a salad apart and get the same ingredients you started with. You cannot take bread apart to get back flour, water and yeast — a chemical change happened in the baking.

items.q: Match each word to the meaning the book gives it.
pairs: A combination of different types of matter that can usually be separated back into its original parts
A specific type of matter made of particles of the same type
The result when two or more types of matter interact to form a new type of matter
A solid formed from a chemical change
items.why: These four are the chapter's Core Vocabulary, and every question in this review turns on one of them. A mixture keeps its parts; a chemical change makes something new that cannot easily be taken apart again.

items.q: An iron chain turns from smooth grey to rough reddish-brown. Why does the book call that a chemical change?
opts: Water and oxygen interacted with the iron to make a new substance
The iron was scratched and dented by years of being pulled over rocks
The iron was painted a different colour by someone else
The iron cooled down and its particles moved much closer
items.why: Water and oxygen in the air interact with the iron to form a new substance, rust. The material in a rusty chain cannot be changed back to iron from rust. We know this is a chemical change because the effect of the change is a new substance with new chemical properties.

items.q: What is the one test the book gives for whether a chemical change has happened?
opts: A new substance has formed, with new properties
The matter has changed shape or been broken smaller
Heat was used at some point during the change
The change happened too quickly to be seen
items.why: A chemical change occurs when two or more types of matter interact to form a new substance that has new properties. That is the test: not heat, not speed, not a change of shape — a new substance.

items.q: Which of these does the book list as evidence that a chemical change has happened? Select every correct answer.
opts: A gas forms
The odour changes
The colour changes
The temperature changes
Light is given off
The matter is broken into smaller pieces
The matter changes shape
items.why: Because the particles are too small to see, we have to look for evidence: a gas forming, a change of odour, a change of colour, a change of temperature, light, or a precipitate. Breaking something smaller or changing its shape is a physical change — the matter is still the same matter.

items.q: A baker mixes yeast and sugar, bubbles form, and a smell fills the kitchen. What is the evidence here?
opts: A gas forming, and an odour that was not there before
A change of colour, and a drop in temperature
A precipitate settling at the bottom of the bowl
Light being given off as the mixture is stirred
items.why: Bubbles form when a baker combines yeast and sugar, and the bubbles of gas make bread rise. A change in odour is evidence of a chemical change. Since the odour was not there to start with, we know there was a chemical change.

items.q: Silver goes dull and dark after a while in the air. What has happened?
opts: It reacted with the air to form a new substance, tarnish
Dust from the room settled on it and can be polished away again
Its particles cooled and packed themselves closer
It absorbed water and became slightly heavier
items.why: Shiny sterling silver metal changes color when it reacts with the air. The chemical change causes a new substance, commonly called tarnish. The change in properties, the change of color, is evidence that a new substance has formed.

items.q: Sort each one by whether it is evidence of a chemical change or of a physical change.
chips: Rust forms on an iron chain
A solid appears where two solutions meet
An ice cube melts into water
Sand is worn from rock by the wind
items.why: The question is always whether a new substance has formed. Rust, heat from a match, a firefly's light and a precipitate all say yes. Melting, crushing and wearing down change the form of the matter and leave it the same matter.

opts: A solid formed from a chemical change
A gas released when a liquid is heated
A liquid left when a solid dissolves
A mixture that can be separated again
items.why: A precipitate is a solid formed from a chemical change — a solid that forms from the combination of two solutions. The solid is a new type of matter with new properties, and it cannot easily be changed back to its original chemicals.

items.q: Fireworks turn solid chemicals into a great deal of gas. What happens to the total weight?
opts: It is exactly the same before and after
It falls, because gas weighs less than a solid
It rises, because the gas takes up more space
It cannot be measured once the gas escapes
items.why: During chemical changes the types of matter change, but just like physical changes the total weight of matter does not change. If you measured the weight of all the chemicals before and after, you would find it is exactly the same. No matter is lost or gained in any chemical change.

items.q: Match each piece of evidence to what it shows.

cells: Iron turns reddish-brown and cannot be turned back
A salad is taken apart into the same vegetables
Fireworks weigh the same before and after burning

items.why: Rust cannot be undone, so a new substance formed. A salad comes apart, so nothing new formed. And the weight being unchanged is the rule that holds for every change, chemical or physical: no matter is lost or gained.

mixture.title: Mixtures and chemical changes
vocab: a combination of different types of matter that can usually be separated back into its original parts
text: When different types of matter mix but each type of matter remains unchanged, it is called a mixture. A mixture can be separated back into its original parts.

Sometimes when two types of matter are mixed, one form of matter will interact with the other. The result is a chemical change. This produces new chemicals with different properties. The original “ingredients” cannot easily be separated again.
A salad is a mixture of things, such as vegetables or fruit. You can take the salad apart and get the same ingredients with which you started.
Bread is a mixture of ingredients that are heated and baked. You cannot take the bread apart to get the same ingredients with which you started.

rust.title: Particles Interact to Form New Matter
vocab: a specific type of matter made of particles of the same type
the result when two or more types of matter interact to form a new type of matter
text: When certain chemicals are put together, the particles they are made of sometimes combine to make a new chemical. When this happens, a chemical change has taken place. A chemical change occurs when two or more types of matter interact to form a new substance that has new properties.

Newly cast iron is usually gray with a smooth surface, but over time the metal can change and become reddish-brown with a rough surface. Water and oxygen in the air interact with the iron to form a new substance, rust. The material in a rusty chain cannot be changed back to iron from rust. We know this is a chemical change because the effect of the change is a new substance with new chemical properties.

evidence.title: Evidence of Chemical Changes
text: New matter forms when the chemicals interact and recombine. This provides more evidence that matter is made up of small particles. Since the particles of matter are too small to be seen, we have to look closely for evidence of a chemical change. So, what evidence do we look for?

gas.title: Formation of Gas, and a change of odour
text: Cars produce exhaust when the engine is running. Exhaust is a gas that forms when an engine burns fuel such as liquid gasoline. The burning releases a set of new chemicals all mixed together as a gas. When a substance is burned, such as fuel, or when it combines with other matter to form a gas, it is often the result of a chemical change.

Another example of gas formation is when a baker combines yeast and sugar. Bubbles form. The bubbles of gas make bread rise. How else can you tell if someone is baking bread? A change in odor is evidence of a chemical change. Baking bread gives off a yummy odor. Since the odor was not there to start with, we know there was a chemical change.

colour.title: Change of Colour, and of Temperature
text: When copper is exposed to air and water for a long time, the copper changes into other chemicals, causing a change in color. The copper changes color because a chemical change has occurred.

Shiny sterling silver metal also changes color when it reacts with the air. The chemical change causes a new substance, commonly called tarnish. The change in properties, the change of color, is evidence that a new substance has formed.

Just like color changes, a change in temperature signals a chemical change. You would never touch the head of a burning match. It is hot! The change in temperature when you light a match tells you that a chemical change has occurred.

precipitate.title: Light, and a precipitate
vocab: a solid formed from a chemical change
text: Have you ever seen tiny flashes of light in the sky at night on a summer evening? If so, you might have seen the light of a lightning bug. Lightning bugs can produce light. The light appears when a chemical change occurs in part of the insect’s body. Those little flashes of light are evidence of a chemical change occurring.

The chemical change shown in this picture of a sink drain forms a precipitate. A precipitate is a solid that forms from the combination of two solutions. The solid is a new type of matter with new properties. The precipitate cannot easily be changed back to its original chemicals. Formation of a precipitate shows that a chemical change has occurred!

conserved.title: Matter Is Conserved During a Chemical Change
text: During chemical changes, the types of matter change. But, just like physical changes, the total weight of matter does not change.

Imagine colorful fireworks lighting up a night sky. Fireworks contain solid chemicals. When the solids burn, they quickly turn to large amounts of gas that take up more space. Since the gas is in a very small tube, pressure builds up. When the pressure releases, you hear a loud bang!

Fireworks are the result of a number of chemical changes. But if you were to measure carefully the weight of all the chemicals before and after, you would discover something interesting. You would have data that shows that the weight of all chemicals before and after a chemical change is exactly the same. No matter is lost or gained in any chemical change.
